title: Risotto al Tartufo Nero
subtitle: Black truffle risotto with Parmesan
excerpt: Risotto al tartufo nero is a plain Parmesan risotto finished with black truffle paste and, if available, shaved fresh black truffle. The truffle perfumes the hot rice as it rests. It is one of the most luxurious pasta dishes in the Italian canon -- and one of the simplest to make.
sourceNotes: Black truffle risotto is associated with Umbria and the Marches, where the Tuber melanosporum (Perigord black truffle) is harvested from late November through March. The dish also appears in northern Italy, particularly Piedmont, where both black and white truffles grow.

content.text: The secret of truffle risotto is that the truffle goes in off the heat, after the butter and Parmesan have been stirred in. The residual heat is enough to perfume the rice. Adding truffle over direct heat destroys most of the aroma. Rest the risotto covered for 2 minutes before serving to let the smell intensify.

Heat {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} of olive oil in a heavy pan over medium heat. Add {{onion}} onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft. Add {{carnaroli-rice}} rice and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in {{white-wine-dry}} wine and stir until absorbed.
Add hot {{chicken-stock}} stock a ladleful at a time, stirring constantly for 18 minutes until the rice is al dente. Season with {{salt-table}} salt.

Remove from the heat. Stir in {{unsalted-butter}} butter and {{parmesan}} Parmesan vigorously. Stir in {{truffle-paste}} truffle paste or shaved fresh truffle. Cover and rest for 2 minutes. Serve immediately in warmed bowls.

items.cause: The truffle was added too early or to a pan that was still over the heat.
items.fix: Add truffle only off the heat. The volatile compounds that give truffle its aroma evaporate quickly when heated. Rest covered for 2 minutes -- the steam inside the pan intensifies the perfume.

content.text: Black truffle risotto is made in Umbria, around Norcia and Spoleto, where black truffles are harvested from late autumn through winter. It also appears in Piedmont, around Alba. White truffle is more prized in Piedmont, but black truffle risotto is made there too. The dish is simple on purpose. Rice and butter carry the truffle without distraction.
